plain_english: Now the first word, of unceasing highest-recognition-nature: to determine it, this second treatise I begin.
sanskrit_cite: yattatrādyaṃ padamaviratānuttarajñaptirūpaṃ tannirṇetuṃ prakaraṇamidamārabhe@haṃ dvitīyam

plain_english: For the means-less, whose nature: what point by teaching here? Once may teaching be; afterwards as means-less it is called.
sanskrit_cite: anupāyaṃ hi yadrūpaṃ ko@rtho deśanayātra vai sakṛtsyāddeśanā paścādanupāyatvamucyayate

plain_english: This means-less reality — whence without means? By itself; but of them that such: what should we say, indeed, to them?
sanskrit_cite: anupāyamidaṃ tattvamityupāyaṃ vinā kutaḥ svayaṃ tu teṣāṃ tattādṛk kiṃ brūmaḥ kila tānprati

plain_english: Which fourfold-told form of awareness — of the pervading, this: own nature alone is to be regarded; for ever-arisen is the pervading.
sanskrit_cite: yaccaturdhoditaṃ rūpaṃ vijñānasya vibhorasau svabhāva eva mantavyaḥ sa hi nityodito vibhuḥ

plain_english: By so many uncounted natures it shines; some part-by-part, others enter partlessly through that.
sanskrit_cite: etāvadbhirasaṃkhyātaiḥ svabhāvairyatprakāśate ke@pyaṃśāṃśikayā tena viśantyanye niraṃśataḥ

plain_english: There too, from means-and-the-rest-expecting otherness-yoga, of means too not to be barred: variety from its otherness.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi cābhyupāyādisāpekṣānyatvayogataḥ upāyasyāpi no vāryā tadanyatvādvicitratā

plain_english: There, who pure-souled, in Bhairavī, own awareness, means-less practicing: whose rule — is proclaimed.
sanskrit_cite: tatra ye nirmalātmāno bhairavīyāṃ svasaṃvidam nirupāyāmupāsīnāstadvidhiḥ praṇigadyate

plain_english: There, for now, rite-yoga does not deserve means-hood; for from that arisen, rather it is distinctly discerned.
sanskrit_cite: tatra tāvatkriyāyogo nābhyupāyatvamarhati sa hi tasmātsamudbhūtaḥ pratyuta pravibhāvyate

plain_english: In awareness, means just would be — quoted; if awareness is called: luminosity in self-luminous — and that, thence, from another — how?
sanskrit_cite: jñaptāvupāya eva syāditi cejjñaptirucyate prakāśatvaṃ svaprakāśe tacca tatrānyataḥ katham

plain_english: Awareness-principle, 'self-luminous' — in this, what? Now, by reasoning: in its absence, would the universe be non-shining from inertia?
sanskrit_cite: saṃvittattvaṃ svaprakāśamityasminkaṃ nu yuktibhiḥ tadabhāve bhavedviśvaṃ jaḍatvādaprakāśakam

plain_english: Whatever means, outer, would be, or inner, whatsoever: it, all face-turned-to-it; there, means-bearing — how?
sanskrit_cite: yāvānupāyo bāhyaḥ syādāntaro vāpi kaścana sa sarvastanmukhaprekṣī tatropāyatvabhākkatham

plain_english: Abandon attentions, now: where, indeed, do you place attention? Discern yourself, it: in the full, attention — not, for, indeed fitting; the unfull does not attain, and, the true nature.
sanskrit_cite: tyajāvadhānāni nanu kva nāma dhatse@vadhānaṃ vicinu svayaṃ tat pūrṇe@vadhānaṃ na hi nāma yuktaṃ nāpūrṇamabhyeti ca satyabhāvam

plain_english: By that attention-vital of this, meditation-and-the-rest, on the higher path, in the Bhairavī: how indeed would there be direct means-ness?
sanskrit_cite: tenāvadhānaprāṇasya bhāvanādeḥ pare pathi bhairavīye kathaṃkāraṃ bhavetsākṣādupāyatā

plain_english: Whoever even by direct means that nature discern: surely they, for sun-awareness, firefly-desiring, are dullards.
sanskrit_cite: ye@pi sākṣādupāyena tadrūpaṃ praviviñcate nūnaṃ te sūryasaṃvittyai khadyotādhitsavo jaḍāḥ

plain_english: And, as long as this outer — inner-means-deemed: that mere luminous-natured alone, Śiva's own form.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ ca yāvadidaṃ bāhyamāntaropāyasaṃmatam tatprakāśātmatāmātraṃ śivasyaiva nijaṃ vapuḥ

plain_english: Blue, yellow, 'pleasure': luminance alone is Śiva; in this supreme nonduality, luminous-natured: what other?
sanskrit_cite: nīlaṃ pītaṃ sukhamiti prakāśaḥ kevalaḥ śivaḥ amuṣminparamādvaite prakāśātmani ko@paraḥ

plain_english: Means-to-be-attained-relation would be luminance alone — for it.
sanskrit_cite: upāyopeyabhāvaḥ syātprakāśaḥ kevalaṃ hi saḥ

plain_english: This — duality indeed — this, difference: this nonduality, thus, even, in the luminous form alone — this shines, the Supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: idaṃ dvaitama@yaṃ bheda idamadvaitamityapi prakāśavapurevāyaṃ bhāsate parameśvaraḥ

plain_english: In this level, pleasure, pain, bondage, release — whether conscious or inert: like pot-and-jar, same-meaning words — of them even just one — and.
sanskrit_cite: asyāṃ bhūmau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bandho mokṣaścitarjaḍaḥ ghaṭakumbhavadekārthāḥ śabdāste@pyekameva ca

plain_english: In the shining-forth, for an unlit part, how, indeed, radiance? In the shining, in that or, that duality of it obliterated.
sanskrit_cite: praśāśe hyaprakāśāṃśaḥ kathaṃ nāma prakāśatām prakāśamāne tasminvā taddvaitāstasya lopitāḥ

plain_english: In non-shining, then, in that or: reality, how is it said? Not luminance-specificity unapproved, indeed it follows.
sanskrit_cite: aprakāśe@tha tasminvā vastutā kathamucyate na prakāśaviśeṣatvamata evopapadyate

plain_english: Hence, 'one luminance' — thus, in the doctrine here, well-established: from afar warded off, truly, the different-knowledge-sayers.
sanskrit_cite: ata ekaprakāśo@yamiti vāde@tra susthite dūrādāvāritāḥ satyaṃ vibhinnajñānavādinaḥ

plain_english: Mere luminance taught through non-shining-denial: of the word 'one', not — but the meaning: is number, bearing consciousness-manifest-difference.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśamātramuditamaprakāśaniṣedhanāt ekaśabdasya na tvarthaḥ saṃkhyā cidvyaktibhedabhāk

plain_english: Not this: śakti, the great goddess; not resting on another, since; nor, and this: śakti-possessing god; not of anyone a resort, since.
sanskrit_cite: naiṣa śaktirmahādevī na paratrāśrito yataḥ na caiṣa śaktimāndevo na kasyāpyāśrayo yataḥ

plain_english: Not this: the meditated, from meditator-hood, not: the meditator, from meditated-absence; no worshipful, from worshipper-absence, from worshipful-absence: no worshipper.
sanskrit_cite: naiṣa dhyeyo dhyātrabhāvānna dhyātā dhyeyavarjanāt na pūjyaḥ pūjakābhāvātpūjyābhāvānna pūjakaḥ

plain_english: Not mantra, nor; and mantra-able, this; not, and the pronouncer, the Lord; no initiation, initiator, or even; no initiated one, the Great Lord.
sanskrit_cite: na mantro na ca mantryo@sau na ca mantrayitā prabhuḥ na dīkṣā dīkṣako vāpi na dīkṣāvānmaheśvaraḥ

plain_english: Place-seat-restraint-offering-mass-invocation-and-the-rest, ending in dismissal: there is not here, in doer-deed-act-abandoned.
sanskrit_cite: sthānāsananirodhārghasaṃghānāvāhanādikam visarjanāntaṃ nāstyatra kartṛkarmakriyojjhite

plain_english: Not being, not not-being, being, not-being: and that, not both-abandoned: hard to know, for, that state: some, whatever, this unsurpassed.
sanskrit_cite: na sanna cāsatsadasanna ca tannobhayojjhitam durvijñeyā hi sāvasthā kimapyetadanuttaram

plain_english: 'This' — thus appearance, for which, being of cut-off nature: it, just, pot-like in the world, situated then: not this is Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite: ayamityavabhāso hi yo bhāvo@vacchidātmakaḥ sa eva ghaṭavalloke saṃstathā naiṣa bhairavaḥ

plain_english: Non-being, and non-shining, not: anywhere usefulness; of the universe, is the life, truly, luminance-natured-alone, and it.
sanskrit_cite: asattvaṃ cāprakāśatvaṃ na kutrāpyupayogitā viśvasya jīvitaṃ satyaṃ prakāśaikātmakaśca saḥ

plain_english: By these two just, but from causes: not two-natured, nor two-abandoned; wholly, for, shines it: by what form, let it be mantred?
sanskrit_cite: ābhyāmeva tu hetubhyāṃ na dvyātmā na dvayojjhitaḥ sarvātmanā hi bhātyeṣa kena rūpeṇa mantryatām

plain_english: In the venerable Triśiras, told, supreme-knowledge-nature, by śakti dwelling within the womb, śakti-wombed, supreme state.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmattriśirasi proktaṃ parajñānasvarūpakam śaktyā garbhāntarvartinyā śaktigarbha paraṃ padam

plain_english: Neither being, nor non-being, nor the pair: by unsayable speech, unsayable-word-escalated, śakti-dwelling, śakti-devoid.
sanskrit_cite: na bhāvo nāpyabhāvo na dvayaṃ vācāmagocarāt akathyapadavīrūḍhaṃ śaktisthaṃ śaktivarjitam

plain_english: Thus, who rooted-knowledge-truth-purified, on the anuttara path, rooted: they, means-unruled.
sanskrit_cite: iti ye rūḍhasaṃvittiparamārthapavitritāḥ anuttarapathe rūḍhāste@bhyupāyāniyantritāḥ

plain_english: Of them, this, shines together, everywhere, the being-circle, standing-forth just, melted in consciousness-Bhairava-fire.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāmidaṃ samābhāti sarvato bhāvamaṇḍalam puraḥsthameva saṃvittibhairavāgnivilāpitam

plain_english: Of these, pleasure-pain-share-doubt-fear-notions, nirvikalpa-entry-only-remainder come to.
sanskrit_cite: eteṣāṃ sukhaduḥkhāṃśaśaṃkātaṃkavikalpanāḥ nirvikalpaparāveśamātraśeṣatvamāgatāḥ

plain_english: Of these, no mantra, no meditation, no worship, nor even imagination: no, from samayin to ācārya, anyone, is a resting-place.
sanskrit_cite: eṣāṃ na mantro na dhyānaṃ na pūjā nāpi kalpanā na samayyādikācāryaparyantaḥ ko@pi viśramaḥ

plain_english: All-restraint-system-break-marks-bearing, not than grace beyond, in any remaining conduct, is the purpose.
sanskrit_cite: samastayantraṇātantratroṭanāṭaṃkadharmiṇaḥ nānugrahātparaṃ kiṃciccheṣavṛttau prayojanam

plain_english: Own, to be done, whatever, considering the world, this, from effort, not, for others' sake, toward, joins, any own activity, but if, whose every existence-stain is destroyed, full of Bhairavī-nature: the deed, his, clearly this just this-much world-duty merely.
sanskrit_cite: svaṃ kartavyaṃ kimapi kalayaṃlloka eṣa prayatnānno pārārthyaṃ prati ghaṭayate kāṃcana svapravṛttim yastu dhvastākhilabhavamalo bhairavībhāvapūrṇaḥ kṛtyaṃ tasya sphuṭamidamiyallokakartavyamātram

plain_english: Him, who see, by that-form-order, stainless-aware, they too, of his form, so much, just, of him, grace-naturedness.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ ye paśyanti tādrūpyakrameṇāmalasaṃvidaḥ te@pi tadrūpiṇastāvatyevāsyānugrahātmatā

plain_english: This tattva-recognition is chief, sacrifice-and-the-rest is called, up to initiation, by the Lord, in the Siddhayogīśvarī doctrine.
sanskrit_cite: etattattvaparijñānaṃ mukhyaṃ yāgādi kathyate dīkṣāntaṃ vibhunā śrīmatsiddhayogīśvarīmate

plain_english: From the altar, the higher, loom, from the loom northward, the cloth, from cloth, meditation, then, the to-be-meditated, then, should be dhāraṇā higher.
sanskrit_cite: sthaṇḍilāduttaraṃ tūraṃ tūrāduttarataḥ paṭaḥ paṭāddhyānaṃ tato dhyeyaṃ tataḥ syāddhāraṇottarā

plain_english: Then too, yoga-born, form, then too, knowledge higher, by knowledge, for, greatly accomplished, should become a Yogīśvara — but, quoted.
sanskrit_cite: tato@pi yogajaṃ rūpaṃ tato@pi jñānamuttaram jñānena hi mahāsiddho bhavedyogīśvarastviti

plain_english: He too, through freedom-abode, if even of the impure-aware, grace, desiring to grace that forthcoming one, he should resort to the rite.
sanskrit_cite: so@pi svātantryadhāmnā cedapyanirmalasaṃvidām anugrahaṃ cikīrṣustadbhāvinaṃ vidhimāśrayet

plain_english: According to the graced one, varied, it, and, is taught, through Parāparā-and-the-rest-means-flood-mixedness-division.
sanskrit_cite: anugrāhyānusāreṇa vicitraḥ sa ca kathyate parāparādyupāyaughasaṃkīrṇatvavibhedataḥ

plain_english: For that purpose alone, and of him too, of the Lord-formed one, that means-scripture-and-the-rest-hearing-studying-zeal.
sanskrit_cite: tadarthameva cāsyāpi parameśvararūpiṇaḥ tadabhyupāyaśāstrādiśravaṇādhyayanādaraḥ

plain_english: For not, of him, of the free, anywhere, wherever, is refutation, not of the impure-minded, of man, grace, but meanslessness.
sanskrit_cite: nahi tasya svatantrasya kāpi kutrāpi khaṇḍanā nānirmalacitaḥ puṃso@nugrahastvanupāyakaḥ

plain_english: In the venerable Ūrmi great-scripture, Siddha-lineage-shaped: this told, so, by the venerable Somānanda and the teachers.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmadūrmimahāśāstre siddhasaṃtānarūpake idamuktaṃ tathā śrīmatsomānandādidaiśikaiḥ

plain_english: From the guru's word-and-the-rest, from wiping by heaped reasoning, from assurance — the śāstra, toward, from the arisen, or even, from the told: when dissolved, in the doubt-cloud, that heart-sky-shining-greatness, of the Lord, sun-like, touching, feet darkness-conquering.
sanskrit_cite: gurorvākyādyuktipracayaracanonmārjanavaśāt samāśvāsācchāstraṃ prati samuditādvāpi kathitāt vilīne śaṃkābhre tdṛdayagaganodbhāsimahasaḥ prabhoḥ sūryasyeva spṛśata caraṇāndhvāntajayinaḥ

plain_english: This anuttara-abode-discerning, means-shed, made: the ahnika.
sanskrit_cite: idamanuttaradhāmavivecakaṃ vigalitaupayikaṃ kṛtamāhnikam
